title: Applicable engineering authoring guidance
description: The Change and quality control contract for selecting and explaining canonical engineering authoring guidance within a declared adopted REM profile. Published capability guidance consumes this contract for the model-authoring branch of a bounded specialist activity; other specialist procedures retain their own owners and support boundaries.

operations.name: select_applicable_authoring_guidance
operations.purpose: Identify which canonical sources and versions govern the requested model-authoring activity and explain their applicability.
inputs: Requested authoring activity, participant context, and the project's declared adopted method/profile version.
Available canonical guidance with identifiable owners and source versions, including previously selected guidance when its applicability is being reconsidered.
outputs: Applicable canonical owners and source versions, selection rationale, and navigation to the relevant concepts, methods, rules, and worked examples.
Explicit unavailable, superseded, incompatible, ambiguous, or inapplicable guidance context, including the affected scope and missing selection or responsible source owner.
behavior: Match the requested activity and declared profile version to their canonical guidance owners; preserve the distinction between governing rules and illustrative explanations or examples.
Keep the selected source version and applicability basis identifiable across human and agent presentations without changing the governing meaning.
After a profile change, disclose previously used material that is incompatible, superseded, or unavailable instead of silently applying it or substituting a different version.
For an activity outside the adopted REM model-authoring scope, explain that this contract is inapplicable and leave the selected specialist procedure with its existing owner.
Identify missing or conflicting guidance and its responsible owner. Selecting guidance neither interprets or migrates the engineering model nor establishes project adoption or permission to edit it.

failure_behavior.condition: The requested activity or adopted profile version is missing or unknown.
failure_behavior.outcome: Identify the missing selection and affected scope without claiming that an authoring method is applicable.

failure_behavior.condition: The selected activity or version has no available authoritative guidance, or its governing sources conflict.
failure_behavior.outcome: Report the unavailable scope or conflicting owners and versions; leave the dependent rule selection unresolved instead of inventing a rule or choosing an incompatible substitute.

operations.name: explain_authoring_or_correction
operations.purpose: Explain the semantic steps, governing rules, expected outcomes, and correction paths for the selected model-authoring activity within its supported scope.
inputs: Requested activity, applicable canonical guidance selection and source versions, and author-provided engineering context.
Existing definitions and identifiable review or validation findings when a correction is requested.
Declared representation support, known authority limits, and unresolved engineering decisions relevant to the requested activity.
outputs: Activity-specific guidance that explains governing rules, semantic authoring or correction steps, expected outcomes, and applicable checks with their authoritative sources.
Explicit unfinished scope, unresolved decisions, unsupported representations or operations, separately authorized actions, and the responsible next clarification or correction.
behavior: Use the applicable canonical method to explain the requested requirement, Scenario, system, architecture, relationship, naming, retirement, or correction activity; preserve each activity's distinct engineering meaning.
Relate a supplied finding to its identifiable diagnostic, owning rule, affected definition, and a correction whose result remains subject to the applicable checks.

Provide sufficient governing content and source navigation for the requested decision; concise explanations must not hide required rules, failure conditions, or obtainable material detail. Distinguish normative rules from examples and structural aids.

When a material engineering decision is unresolved, explain the dependency and the highest-value clarification needed at that time without concealing other uncertainty or supplying an invented answer.

Explain available conceptual guidance when a representation is unsupported or an action requires separate authority, while leaving the dependent action unperformed and avoiding conformance or permission claims.

Keep recommendations distinct from edits, conformant records, approved changes, verification observations, and satisfied requirements. Published capability guidance retains execution, artifact/output composition, actual scope reporting, and local handoff under the applicable specialist contract.

Preserve source applicability, current authoritative vocabulary, and privacy limits. Do not require secrets, credentials, raw private environment data, or unrelated machine-local information to explain the method.

failure_behavior.condition: Applicable guidance, required subject context, or a material engineering decision is unavailable or conflicting.
failure_behavior.outcome: Identify the affected unfinished scope and responsible clarification or correction owner; keep dependent conclusions unsettled while explaining only the supported scope.

failure_behavior.condition: The requested format or operation is retired, unsupported, or not adopted, or the requested action lacks established applicable authority.
failure_behavior.outcome: Explain the support or authority boundary and any available conceptual guidance. Leave the dependent action unperformed without reviving a retired operation, claiming format conformance, or deciding authority through guidance.

consistency_rules: Guidance selection and explanation refer to the same applicable activity, profile, and identifiable canonical source versions. A changed or unresolved selection must remain visible rather than silently mixing incompatible rules.
Human and agent presentations preserve the same governing meaning. Canonical rules remain at their owning sources; guidance does not create a competing policy copy or turn an example into authority.

An explanation is not artifact mutation, model interpretation or migration, adoption, an authority determination, independent assessment, or requirement satisfaction. Partial and blocked guidance must remain distinguishable from a complete usable specialist result.

The contract covers the adopted REM model-authoring alternative in SCN-053. It does not substitute a universal procedure for the full set of published specialist activities or establish successful capability execution.

For requirement-first consumption by MOD-012, canonical method selection distinguishes requirement validity, System Design completeness and architectural allocation; it supplies the three authoring methods without adding per-method approval gates.
compatibility_rules: The declared adopted profile and its canonical owners govern the supported activities, representations, rule vocabulary, and applicable versions. Unknown or incompatible context cannot be treated as a supported fallback.

A published capability consumer must preserve source applicability, required rule coverage, privacy, stop conditions, and claim limits when composing the explanation into its own specialist output and handoff.

This logical contract introduces no agent runtime, transport, public command, wire format, automatic model migration, or installed-skill adoption. Detailed published specialist contracts retain their existing authority and support boundaries.

Guidance usefulness assessment, action-authority decisions, and assurance judgments have separate responsibilities; defining this contract does not complete their collaboration or allocated-requirement analysis.

sources.basis: Derive the Governance-to-published-capability interaction for the Scenario's adopted REM model-authoring alternative. Preserve specialist ownership, usable scoped output, source applicability, supported stops, and the distinction between partial work and completion; this does not define every published specialist protocol.

Derive selection and explanation operations from the existing canonical authoring guidance behavior. MOD-008 retains those Function allocations and semantic responsibilities while MOD-017 accounts for this external contract. Neither this ownership nor consumption by MOD-012 creates new authority, runtime realization, or satisfaction evidence.
Draft integrated design from the accepted requirement-first basis. This defines target responsibility and cooperation, not installed capability, design approval, runtime evidence or SQLite adoption.
